classification.difficultyReason: Foundation: students locate the highest and lowest observations, read the 4 am value and apply the explicitly taught midpoint interpolation at 9 am and 1 pm. The hardest demand directly follows the guided temperature example.

content.prompt: Consider the following graph, which shows the outside temperature over a 24-hour period that starts at midnight.

spec.description: Temperature during a day; red connected segments with blue circular markers, rectangular reading grid, arrowed axes, diagonal time labels and italic axis titles.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no answer annotations.

children.label: a
children.prompt: When was the hottest time of the day?

answer.worked: The highest plotted point is at 2 pm, at approximately $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: When was the coolest time of the day?

answer.short: 12 am at the start of the 24-hour period.
answer.worked: The lowest plotted point is the starting midnight, at approximately $6^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The final midnight is approximately $7^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use the graph to estimate the temperature at these times of the day.

answer.worked: At 4 am, the plotted point is at approximately $10^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
9 am is halfway between 8 am and 10 am. Read halfway along the connecting segment, between approximately $16^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$: approximately $18^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
1 pm is halfway between noon and 2 pm. Read halfway along the connecting segment, between approximately $23^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$: approximately $24^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
